body:
Bubble Sort has the following time complexities:

- **Best Case: O(n)** - When the array is already sorted, only one pass is needed with the optimized version.
- **Average Case: O(n²)** - On average, we need n/2 passes with n/2 comparisons each.
- **Worst Case: O(n²)** - When the array is sorted in reverse order, every element needs to be compared and swapped.

Think of it like sorting playing cards. In each round, the largest unsorted card 'bubbles up' to its correct position. So for n cards, you need at most n-1 rounds, and in each round you compare adjacent pairs. That gives O(n²) for worst/average case. Best case O(n) if you add a flag to detect no swaps.
Best O(n), Worst and Average O(n^2). Space complexity is O(1) since it's in-place.
